newsitem.title: USA: American's release from N.Korea said on track.
newsitem.headline: American's release from N.Korea said on track.

text.p: U.S. congressman Bill Richardson's talks in North Korea on the release of a detained American are going well and he is expected to fly to Japan with the detainee within hours, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Richardson, a New Mexico Democrat, and Carl Hunziker, who has been held in North Korea since Aug. 24, were expected to arrive around 10.30 p.m. EST (0330 GMT Wednesday) at Yokota air base near Tokyo.

Burns gave no clear explanation of why Richardson, who had originally planned to leave North Korea 24 hours earlier, had postponed his departure. But he denied reports that a hitch had developed in the plan to win Hunziker's freedom.
Richardson had agreed to a North Korean request to extend his stay in Pyongyang by one day, he said without elaborating.
"We understand that Congressman Richardson's efforts with the North Koreans on the release of Mr Hunziker are going well," Burns told a news briefing.
He described as "unsubstantiated" and "clearly not accurate" reports from Japan quoting U.S. sources as saying complications had arisen in the talks.
"We're very hopeful that when Congressman Richardson returns in just a couple of hours from now...to Yokota air force base in Japan that he will have with him Mr Carl Hunziker," Burns said.
"We canot be assured of that, obviously, until the plane departs Pyongyang."
Burns said the release of Hunziker, who was arrested after crossing the Yalu River from China into North Korea, was Richardson's sole aim in flying to Pyongyang Monday.
North Korea has said it "proved by investigation" that Hunziker, 26, was a U.S. spy.
Hunziker's family has denied the charge, saying he is a missionary. U.S. and South Korean officials have denied that Hunziker was spying for their countries.

Burns declined comment on reports that Hunziker's family had agreed to pay North Korea for Hunziker's release, but a senior U.S. official said it was "very clear (the North Koreans) have asked for a cash payment."

The official gave no figures. The Washington Post quoted Hunziker's father Edwin, who lives in Parkland, Wa., as saying the family had agreed to pay $5,000 for the detainee's "room and board", following an initial North Korean demand for $100,000.
